Installing turf on Kissimmee's sand, water table and paperwork

Kissimmee is home base, the town this crew starts every route from. A residential lawn here runs $8–$18 per square foot installed as of September 2026, but the build changes with the parcel: whether it sits inside city limits or unincorporated Osceola County, how close it is to Lake Tohopekaliga, and which Toho Water watering day applies to the address.

Reviewed by Luis Austin, owner · Last reviewed September 21, 2026

What's different about a turf install in Kissimmee

Kissimmee is the county seat of Osceola County, and the address on a lot does more than set a mailing ZIP. A parcel inside the city limits gets its permit reviewed by the city; a lot a few streets over, still carrying a Kissimmee mailing address, often sits in unincorporated Osceola County, where a separate county office does the same job. Toho Water Authority controls two irrigation mornings or evenings a week here, the native ground is fine sand with a water table that climbs close to the surface for weeks each summer, and the housing stock ranges from a downtown built on the shore of Lake Tohopekaliga in 1883 to phases of Tohoqua still being framed in 2026. Along US-192, whole subdivisions are zoned for nightly rentals under the county's short-term-rental overlay, which changes what a vacation rental turf crew plans for before ever pricing the job. None of that moves the $8–$18 per square foot range for a residential lawn; it moves the base, the paperwork, and where the state's ten-foot waterbody setback actually falls on the lot.

Does the City of Kissimmee or Osceola County review your permit?

It depends on the parcel, not the envelope. Most addresses inside the city limits go through the City of Kissimmee's Development Services Building Division, reached at 407-518-2379 or permitting@kissimmee.gov, which reviews site and landscape work including turf conversions (permitting process). A good share of properties that say "Kissimmee, FL" on the mail are in unincorporated Osceola County instead, where the county's Building Division handles the same review at 407-742-0200, with records searchable online through Accela Citizen Access. The fastest way to settle which office applies to one specific address is the Osceola County Property Appraiser's parcel search, cross-checked against the county's own zoning designation lookup; both show whether a parcel falls inside the city boundary. Full detail on what each office wants on paper is at permit rules for the City of Kissimmee and permit rules for unincorporated Osceola County.

What does Toho Water's schedule and Kissimmee's sandy soil mean for a lawn?

Toho Water Authority, which serves Kissimmee and most of Osceola County, limits irrigation to two mornings or evenings a week: odd-numbered addresses on Wednesday and Saturday, even-numbered addresses on Thursday and Sunday, with no daytime watering allowed (Toho's watering-day rules). Kissimmee sits in the Kissimmee Basin that the South Florida Water Management District manages, part of the same chain of lakes that starts at Lake Tohopekaliga (Upper Kissimmee Basin water supply plan). Underneath most yards sits fine sand from the Myakka, Immokalee, Smyrna and Basinger series, poorly to very poorly drained soils where the water table typically sits twenty to forty inches down for months and can climb within a couple of feet of the surface during the wettest weeks of summer. That pairing, tight watering days above ground and a shallow water table below it, is part of why the adopted state turf standard bans in-ground irrigation on synthetic turf and calls for a washed, open-graded rock base: a lawn here has to shed water on its own, since it isn't getting rinsed by a sprinkler on the other five days of the week.

Which Kissimmee neighborhoods need extra planning?

Downtown Kissimmee grew up on the north shore of Lake Tohopekaliga after the city incorporated in 1883, and the historic downtown core still carries mature live oaks and older lots close to the water, where the setback and drip-line rules both apply before excavation starts. Golf-adjacent lots around Remington Golf Club, open since 1996, and gated, ARC-reviewed communities such as Bellalago on the lake and the newer Tohoqua off Neptune Road add a design-review step most jobs skip entirely. Along US-192, the county's short-term-rental overlay runs a district near the theme parks and another closer to the Turnpike, covering resort-style communities where a yard gets turned over between guests instead of mowed on a weekly rotation. Compare notes with a neighbor in St. Cloud or Buenaventura Lakes and the permit answer can differ block to block; Florida law still lets an HOA require design review, it just can't ban turf that isn't visible from the frontage.

How do you pick the best turf installer near me in Kissimmee?

Two questions matter here more than a sales pitch does. First, who is actually filing the paperwork on this job, City Hall, the county's Building Division, or a community's architectural review committee, since a contractor who hasn't asked which one applies to the address hasn't done the homework yet. Second, how the quote treats a lot backing onto a lake, canal or drainage swale: an installer who mentions the ten-foot setback and the drip-line rule without being asked has clearly built the state standard into the estimate rather than finding out about it midway through the job.

Questions people ask

Is a Kissimmee mailing address the same as the city limits?

Not always. Osceola County's largest city sits inside its own boundary, but plenty of addresses reading "Kissimmee, FL" sit in unincorporated Osceola County next door. The county Property Appraiser's parcel search and the county's zoning designation lookup both show which office actually reviews a permit for a given parcel.

How many days a week can I run a sprinkler on new sod here?

Toho Water Authority allows two irrigation days a week for residential accounts, tied to the address: odd numbers water Wednesday and Saturday, even numbers Thursday and Sunday, with no daytime watering. New sod struggles on that schedule in the dry season; established turf never touches the sprinkler at all, since the adopted state rule bars in-ground irrigation on synthetic turf outright.

Can my Kissimmee HOA say no to a backyard nobody can see from the street?

Under Florida Statute 720.3045, an association can't restrict artificial turf that isn't visible from the parcel's frontage or an adjacent lot, so a fenced backyard behind a home in a gated community is generally protected. A front yard is a different conversation, and the community's design review still applies to the paperwork.

Does turf near Lake Tohopekaliga need special permission?

In one specific way, yes. The adopted state turf rule keeps synthetic turf at least ten feet from a natural or man-made waterbody, which covers Lake Tohopekaliga, East Lake Tohopekaliga, Shingle Creek and the canals linking them, unless a seawall or bulkhead already separates the yard from the water.

What soil should a crew expect to dig into here?

Most Kissimmee lots sit on Myakka, Immokalee, Smyrna or Basinger fine sand, USDA series known for a water table that rises within twenty to forty inches of the surface for months at a stretch. That's why the base calls for washed, open-graded rock instead of compacted fill: a tight base traps water the soil is already holding.
